newsitem.title: UK: ScotAm says considering bid from Prudential.
newsitem.headline: ScotAm says considering bid from Prudential.

text.p: Mutually-owned life assurance company Scottish Amicable said on Wednesday it was considering an offer for the company from Prudential Corporation.

ScotAm, which is already subject to an offer from Abbey National said it would seek competing offers from other parties, including Abbey and had postponed sending out a circular on its own flotation plans for at least two weeks.
ScotAm says considering bid from Prudential
Sandy Stewart, chairman of ScotAm said: "From the outset, the Board has acted solely in the best interests of policyholders and we will continue to work to deliver the best result for them."
The board of ScotAm had come in for sharp criticism in recent days for its reluctance to postpone its plans to drop its mutual status and float the group or discuss Abbey's bid.
Prudential has offered 400 million pounds ($641.3 million) in cash or shares and said it would inject 1.1 billion pounds into ScotAm's life fund.
Abbey's bid valued the group at up to 1.4 billion pounds and included an immediate 400 million pounds minimum payout to policyholders in cash or Abbey shares.
